NOZOMI_QUERY_SCOPE.description: Nozomi Guardian Open Query surface selector (case-insensitive 'assets' / 'alerts' / 'vulns' / 'vulnerabilities' / 'all'). Optional; empty / blank / unknown values walk all three surfaces (the typical operational mode for first-time imports). 'vulns' is an operator-friendly alias for the canonical Nozomi query keyword 'vulnerabilities'. Selected surfaces are walked in the canonical order assets -> alerts -> vulnerabilities. The surface keyword is emitted verbatim into the Nozomi Open Query DSL as `query=<surface> | head N | skip M` against GET /api/open/query/do. Useful for sharding inventory pulls across multiple discovery profiles so one dispatcher agent walks only assets, a second only alerts, and a third only vulnerabilities. Whitespace is trimmed.

NOZOMI_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional Faraday severity floor (case-insensitive 'info' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical'); records whose mapped severity is strictly below the floor are dropped client-side after the fetch. Asset records (no severity of their own) are bucketed from the Nozomi criticality field (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info, or 0..4 numeric); alerts use the published severity field directly (label or 0..10 numeric, falling back to risk when severity is missing); vulnerabilities use severity directly with a fallback to cvss_score / score. Closed / Resolved / Muted / Suppressed / Dismissed / Acknowledged / Mitigated / Accepted-Risk records are floored to 'info' regardless of the published bucket (preserved via an explicit Nozomi-Status pivot). Operator-friendly aliases are accepted ('informational' -> 'info', 'moderate' -> 'medium', 'crit' -> 'critical', 'elevated' -> 'high', 'severe' -> 'critical', 'none' -> 'info'). Blank / missing / unparseable values keep every record (the typical operational mode for first-time imports).

name: nozomi_guardian
title: Nozomi Networks Guardian / CMC
description: Nozomi Networks Guardian / CMC OT / ICS asset, alert, and vulnerability importer. Pulls device inventory, security alerts, and CVE-attributed vulnerability findings from a Nozomi Guardian appliance (or a federated Central Management Console / CMC fan-out) via its Open Query REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Nozomi Guardian is a passive OT / ICS network-monitoring platform — it fingerprints industrial endpoints (PLCs, RTUs, HMIs, historians, jump hosts, IT-side endpoints that touch the OT segment) from mirrored / SPAN traffic and surfaces the resulting asset inventory, rule-based / anomaly alerts, and CVE-attributed vulnerability findings via a single Open Query REST surface keyed on a Nozomi-specific query language ('assets' / 'alerts' / 'vulnerabilities' — each appended with the `| head N | skip M` pagination operators). Endpoint used: GET /api/open/query/do?query=<surface> | head N | skip M; canonical envelope {'result': [...], 'total': N} (note the singular 'result' key — Nozomi's documented Open Query shape) with federated mirrors also exposing {'results': [...]} / {'data': [...]} / {'items': [...]} / {'assets': [...]} / {'alerts': [...]} / {'vulnerabilities': [...]} — all shapes are accepted. Asset records carry id, name, ip, mac_address, vendor, product_name (model), firmware_version, os, type (PLC / RTU / HMI / Historian / Engineering Workstation / IT — Nozomi's published asset taxonomy), level (numeric 0..4 Purdue level), criticality (critical / high / medium / low / none label or 0..4 numeric), zone_id / zone_name, site_id / site_name, first_activity_time / last_activity_time, risk (0..10), and an optional cve_list / vulnerabilities list. Alert records carry id, name / type_name, description, severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info label or 0..10 numeric), type_id (Nozomi's published alert taxonomy: SIGN:NETWORK:MALWARE / SIGN:PROTOCOL:ANOMALY / VI:UNAUTHORIZED-COMMAND etc), status (open / acknowledged / closed / muted / resolved), record_created_at / record_updated_at, src_ip / dst_ip, risk, and zone_id / zone_name. Vulnerability records carry id, cve_id / cve, name, description, severity / cvss_score, node_id (asset id keyed on the finding), node_label (asset name), node_ip (asset IP), zone_id / zone_name, record_created_at / record_updated_at, and an optional status (open / resolved / mitigated / accepted_risk). Auth: Nozomi Guardian's Open Query surface uses HTTP Basic Auth — the dispatcher sends Authorization: Basic <base64(NOZOMI_USER:NOZOMI_PASSWORD)> on every /api/open/ request, with no separate login round-trip. NOZOMI_HOST is the appliance base URL (Guardian / CMC is an on-prem appliance so there is no global default — the executor exits cleanly when missing); whitespace is trimmed and https:// is added when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Pagination is one-based: page=1 -> skip=0, page=2 -> skip=N, walks until len(records) < page_size or the env-only NOZOMI_PAGES knob is reached (default 10, clamped to [1, 100]). 401 short-circuits the whole executor (credentials are wrong); 403 / 429 / 5xx stop pagination on the affected surface and return what we have. Each Nozomi record becomes one Faraday host. Asset records project ip onto host.ip (loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are skipped, falling back to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel), name / label onto host.hostnames, mac_address onto host.mac, and the vendor / product_name / os / firmware_version chain joins onto host.os; the asset itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so OT inventory entries land alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Armis, Axonius, Device42, Fleet, runZero, Jamf Pro). Alert records are keyed on the first usable src_ip / source_ip / dst_ip / destination_ip / ip / node_ip field (falling back to related_assets / related_devices, then 0.0.0.0 for policy-shaped alerts not keyed on any single asset); the alert title (name / type_name / title) lands on host.hostnames and the description / severity / type_id enrichment is embedded in the vulnerability description. Vulnerability records are keyed on node_ip (falling back to ip / asset_ip, then 0.0.0.0); the node_label lands on host.hostnames and the CVE / severity / cvss_score enrichment is embedded in the vulnerability description. Severity bucketing: assets use the criticality field (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info label or 0..4 numeric, falling back to 0..10 for federated mirrors); alerts use severity directly (label or 0..10 numeric, falling back to risk); vulnerabilities use severity directly with a fallback to cvss_score / score. Closed / Resolved / Muted / Suppressed / Dismissed / Acknowledged / Mitigated / Accepted-Risk records are floored to 'info' regardless of the published severity (preserved via an explicit Nozomi-Status pivot). Unparseable / missing severity defaults to 'info'. Status is always 'open' so the operator's remediation workflow takes over; the closed state is preserved via the info-severity floor + the Nozomi-Status pivot. Refs include explicit Nozomi-AssetID / Nozomi-AlertID / Nozomi-VulnID / Nozomi-Zone / Nozomi-Site / Nozomi-Type / Nozomi-Level / Nozomi-Criticality / Nozomi-Vendor / Nozomi-Model / Nozomi-Firmware / Nozomi-Risk / Nozomi-Severity / Nozomi-TypeID / Nozomi-TypeName / Nozomi-Category / Nozomi-Status / Nozomi-CVSS / Nozomi-NodeID / Nozomi-NodeLabel / Nozomi-NodeIP / Nozomi-FirstSeen / Nozomi-LastSeen / Nozomi-CreatedAt / Nozomi-UpdatedAt pivots, plus the canonical NVD CVE permalink for any CVE ids surfaced in the cve_id / cve_list / vulnerabilities / description / title fields. Tags: [nozomi_guardian, ot-security, asset|alert|vuln].
